builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding
summary: Replaces draft-model-free speculative decoding methods (and the need for a separate draft model) by reusing early-layer bonus logits for cheap multi-step draft-tree exploration while final-layer logits verify and correct paths in a low-frequency outer loop. Costs a one-shot fine-tuning pass for the bonus logits, plus implementation complexity in tree construction and state reuse; it adds no extra deployment parameters and claims negligible runtime overhead. It can fail when the fine-tuned early-layer logits miscalibrate on domain-shifted workloads, when GPU memory pressure from tree verification erodes gains, and it is unusable for models accessed only through third-party APIs since it requires access to internal layer activations.
rationale: The claimed speedup is meaningful for a single-GPU setup serving self-hosted open-weight models, but the one-shot fine-tuning dependency and the need to modify the inference stack make workload-specific validation necessary before production adoption.
technique: Early-layer hierarchical speculative decoding with bonus logits

claims.statement: Replaces draft-model-free speculative decoding methods (and the need for a separate draft model) by reusing early-layer bonus logits for cheap multi-step draft-tree exploration while final-layer logits verify and correct paths in a low-frequency outer loop. Costs a one-shot fine-tuning pass for the bonus logits, plus implementation complexity in tree construction and state reuse; it adds no extra deployment parameters and claims negligible runtime overhead. It can fail when the fine-tuned early-layer logits miscalibrate on domain-shifted workloads, when GPU memory pressure from tree verification erodes gains, and it is unusable for models accessed only through third-party APIs since it requires access to internal layer activations.
Reported 2.4x to 2.9x speedup over state-of-the-art draft-model-free speculative decoding baselines, with higher mean accepted tokens, across diverse benchmarks.
